x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as envoy to China.

s: In which language was Ibn Battuta's travelogue Rihla written?
x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla is in Arabic and records the postal system, sati and slave markets.

s: Where was the historian Ferishta born?
x: Ferishta was born at Astarabad in 1552.

s: In which year did Ibn Battuta come to Delhi?
x: Ibn Battuta reached Delhi in 1333 and stayed in India till 1342.

s: At which place was Ibn Battuta born?
x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco in 1304.

s:
Match the following authors with their works:
List I
List II
a. Al-Biruni
I. Tariqh-i-Firoz Shahi
b. Minhaj-us-Siraj
II. Tahqiq-i-Hind
c. Ziauddin Barani
III. The Rihla
d. Ibn Battuta
IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri

s: 'Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi' was written by
x: Tarikh-i- Firuz Shahi is historical account of the reign of Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq. Shams Siraj Afif has written this account. Ziauddin Barani has also written history of Tughlaq dynasty under the same name as Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi.

s: Who is the author of "Tarikh-i-Firujshahi"?
x: The correctly matched list is as follows : Tarikh-i-Hind Al-Biruni Tarikh-i-Delhi Khusrau Rihla Ibn Battuta Tabqat-i-Nasiri Minhaj-us-Siraj (Minhaj-i-Siraj)

s: Which one of the following travelogues has given an insight on the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq?
o: Francois Bernier’s Travels in the Mogul Empire
x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla was written during his stay in India (1333-1342) under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, so it throws light on that reign. Bernier, Manucci and Tavernier were Mughal-era travellers.

s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order.

I. Fatwa-I – Jahandari

II. Prithviraj – Raso

III. Kitab-ul-hind

IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x: The chronological order is Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030), Prithviraj Raso (late 12th c.), Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260), then Fatawa-i-Jahandari (14th c.), which gives III, II, IV, I.

s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Fatawa-i-Jahandari
2. Prithviraja-Raso
3. Kitab-ul-Hind
4. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
Codes:
x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari was written by Ziauddin Barani. Prithviraja-Raso is written by Chandarbardai, Kitab-ul-hind is written by Al-Biruni & Tabaqat-i-Nasiri by Minhaz-i-siraj. Hence correct option is option (d).

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi — Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi
x: Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, not Futuh-us-Salatin. Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami, while both Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote works titled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Which of the following pairs (author – work) is correctly matched?
x: Ibn Battuta wrote the Rihla. Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind, Minhaj-us-Siraj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Isami the Futuh-us-Salatin.

s: Who wrote the Tughluq Nama?
x: Tughluq Nama, like Miftah-ul-Futuh and Ashika, is Amir Khusrau's work; Firdausi wrote the Shahnama.

s: Who wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari?
x: Ziauddin Barani, a nadim of Muhammad bin Tughlaq who wrote under Firoz Tughlaq, wrote both works.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (text – period of composition)?
x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari belongs to the fourteenth century; the other three dates are correct.

s: Who wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, a history of Aibak's reign?
x: Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir on Aibak's reign.

s: Who is the author of Futuh-us-Salatin, written under Bahmani patronage?
x: Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin under Bahmani patronage.

s: Who wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, a history of the Sayyid period?
x: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi on the Sayyid period.

s:
Consider the following statements about Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi:
1. Both Ziauddin Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote works with this title.
2. Shams Siraj Afif's work covers the reign of Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The title has two authors, Barani and Afif; Afif's work covers Firoz Tughlaq's reign, while Barani's runs from Balban to early Firoz.

s: Which of the following was written by Amir Khusrau?
x: Tughluq Nama is by Amir Khusrau. Tarikh-i-Subuktigin is Baihaqi's, Shahnama is Firdausi's and Mitakshara is Vijnaneshvara's.

s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these texts?
1. Chandayan
2. Kitab-ul-Hind
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
4. Prithviraj Raso
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030), Prithviraj Raso (late 12th c.), Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260), Chandayan (1379).

s: Which of the following texts is the earliest?
x: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030) is older than Minhaj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260) and the 14th-century works of Barani and Isami.

s: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Ferishta, also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi?
x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) was written by Muhammad Qasim Ferishta.

s: At the court of which ruler did Ferishta write his history?
o: Ahmad Shah I of the Bahmanis
Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda
x: Ferishta wrote at Bijapur under Ibrahim Adil Shah, naming the work Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi after him.

s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as one of the earliest poets to use the emerging Hindavi (early Urdu) for poetic and devotional expression. He composed Sufi poetry in both Persian and Hindavi and introduced musical forms such as qaul in qawwali, which incorporated this mixed vernacular language.

s: Who among the following wrote the book 'Khazainul-Futuh'?
x: Khazain-ul-Futuh, on Alauddin Khalji's conquests, was written by Amir Khusrau. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir and Minhaj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
x: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was Amir Khusrau. He compiled several verses in Urdu. He is also known as the originator of Qawwali.

s: The savant of both languages “Hindi and Persian” was –
x: Khusrau was a scholar of both the Hindi (Hindavi) and the Persian languages.

s: Father of new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi or Hindustani style was :
x: Amir Khusrau is considered as the father of the new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi” or Hindustani style. He called himself ‘Tuti-i-Hind; He used to say that “Na Lafze Hindiwast aj Farsi Kam” which means the words of Hindi are not less than those of the Persian.

s: Who among the following was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry?
x: Amir Khusrau was a prolific classical poet associated with the Royal courts of more than seven rulers of Delhi Sultanate. He was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry.

s: Amir Khusrau, the “Parrot of India,” was born at-
x: 5. Who among the following called himself the ‘Parrot of India’ ? (a) Qutban (b) Usman (c) Amir Khusrau (d) Amir Hasan U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013 Ans. (c) 6. Amir Khusrau played a pioneering role in the development of – (a) Braj Bhasha (b) Awadhi (c) Khari Boli (d) Bhojpuri U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2008 U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2002 Ans. (c) Amir Khusrau learned various Indian dialects, especially Hindavi, which he loved most. He referred to himself as a 'Turkish-Indian'. He played a pioneering role in the development of Khari Boli.

s: Who among the following is called the ‘Sadi of India’?
x: Amir Hasan-i-Dehlavi is called the ‘Sadi of India’ (Sadi-i- Hind) for his great Ghazals.

s: Which of the following is not associated with the Bhakti Movement?
x: The full name of Amir Khusrau was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau. He was a great poet and scholar of his time. He was not related to the Bhakti Movement. Qiran-us-Sadain, Miftah-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Ashiqa, Tughluq Nama and Khazain-ul-Futuh are some of the main texts composed by him. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu founded Madhyagauriya sect. Guru Nanak was born in a Khatri family in Punjab (Pakistan). He imagined the shapeless form of God. Vallabhacharya was the second saint of Krishnamargi branch.

s: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of Hindi Khari Boli?
x: Amir Khusrau is known as the father of Hindi Khari Boli. He was a promoter of new poetic style ‘Sabak-i-Hindi’ or ‘Hindustani Style.’

s: Amir Khusrau played a pioneer role in the development of
x: Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli, as his Hindavi verses and riddles led to Rekhta/Urdu. So Khari Boli is correct.

s: Amir Khusrau was court poet of
x: Khusrau served several Sultans and is linked with Alauddin's court, which gave him the title Tuti-i-Hind. Alauddin is the best match among the options; Ibrahim Lodi is outside his period.

s: Who among the following called himself the ‘parrot of India’?
x: Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) was the title of Amir Khusrau. Sadi-i-Hind is Amir Hasan's title, so Amir Hasan is the tempting wrong option.

s: Who among the following was the author of Tarikh-i-Alai, which contains the details of the first few years of Sultan Alauddin Khilji?
x: Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh (Khazain-ul-Futuh-i-Alai) describes Alauddin's conquests, so he is the contemporary author. Barani and Afif wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Amir Khusrau was a –
x: Amir Khusrau was a poet, historian, and musician. He was nicknamed as “Tuti-i-Hind.” He was a promoter of Khari Boli of Hindi.

s: “Every pearl in the Royal crown is the crystallised drops of blood fallen from the tearful eyes of the poor peasants” … Who made this statement?
x: The statement is attributed to Amir Khusrau, who criticised the burden on the peasants. The notes do not state this fact.

s: Amir Khusrau was born in
x: Khusrau was born at Patiyali, which lies in the Etah district, so Etah is correct.

s:
Which of the following texts are written by Amir Khusrau ?
1. Khazain-ul-Futuh
2. Nuh Siphir
3. Miftah-ul-Futuh
4. Qiraan-us-Sadain
x: Amir Khusrau composed the following works: • Khaza'in-ul-Futuh • Nuh Sipihr • Miftah-ul-Futuh • Qiran-us-Sa'dain

s: Who gave Amir Khusrau the title Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India)?
x: His patron Alauddin Khalji called him Tuti-i-Hind.

s: In which language did Amir Khusrau write riddles and poetry that later developed into Rekhta or Urdu?
x: Khusrau wrote riddles and poetry in Hindavi, which later developed into Rekhta or Urdu.

s: Amir Khusrau is associated with the development of which style of Persian poetry?
x: Amir Khusrau is credited with founding the Indian style of Persian poetry known as Sabak-i-Hindi or the Hindustani style.

s: Amir Khusrau was given which of the following titles?
x: Amir Khusrau was called Tuti-i-Hind, the Parrot of India. Homer of the East refers to Firdausi, Andhra Bhoja to Krishnadevaraya and Kaviraja to Samudragupta.

s: Which one of the following works of Amir Khusrau deals with the conquests of Alauddin Khalji, including those in the Deccan?
x: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the conquests of Alauddin Khalji, including his Deccan campaigns.

s: What does Amir Khusrau's Qiran-us-Sadain describe?
o: The meeting of Bughra Khan and his son Kaiqubad
x: Qiran-us-Sadain describes the meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad; Miftah-ul-Futuh covers Jalaluddin's campaigns and Nuh Sipihr Mubarak Shah's reign.

s: What does the work Ashiqa, also known as Deval Rani–Khizr Khan, deal with?
o: The meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad
The romance involving Alauddin Khalji’s son
x: Ashiqa, or Deval Rani–Khizr Khan, deals with the romance involving Alauddin Khalji’s son.

s: Whose campaigns does Amir Khusrau's Miftah-ul-Futuh describe?
x: Miftah-ul-Futuh deals with Jalaluddin Khalji's campaigns; Khazain-ul-Futuh deals with Alauddin's.

s: With whose reign does Amir Khusrau's Nuh Sipihr deal?
x: Nuh Sipihr describes Mubarak Shah's reign and praises India.

s: Under which Sultan was Amir Khusrau the poet laureate?
x: Khusrau got the title Tuti-i-Hind from Alauddin but was poet laureate under Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

s: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Chishti saint?
x: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

s: What was the real name of Amir Khusrau?
x: Amir Khusrau's real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau; he was born at Patiyali.

s: Which work of Amir Khusrau describes the rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq?
x: Khusrau's Tughluqnama deals with the rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

s:
Consider the following statement about Ziauddin Barani.

I. He was born in Golconda.

II. He was contemporary of Muhammad bin Tughluq.

III. He wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Barani was a companion of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, so II and III are correct. The notes do not say he was born in Golconda, so statement I is not supported.

s: According to Ziauddin Barani, which model did kingship (jahandari) follow, resting on awe and force?
x: Barani held that jahandari followed the Persian model; he also wanted high office kept for the high-born.

s: What were the state laws called through which the Delhi Sultans governed in practice, leading Barani to deny that the state was truly Islamic?
x: The Sultan was expected to protect the sharia but governed through zawabit (state laws), so Barani did not regard the state as truly Islamic.

s: Whose nadim (companion) was Ziauddin Barani?
x: Barani was the nadim of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote under Firoz Tughlaq.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ziauddin Barani:
1. He held that high office should go only to the high-born.
2. He wrote his works under the patronage of Alauddin Khalji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Barani opposed promoting low-born men; he wrote under Firoz Tughlaq, not Alauddin.

s: Who among the following witnessed the reign of Seven Sultans of Delhi?
x: Amir Khusrau served at the courts of seven successive Delhi Sultans; he was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

s: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi was refused an audience by Nizamuddin Auliya?
x: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya saw the regime of more than seven Sultans, but he never visited their court. Sultan Jalaluddin tried to meet Nizamuddin Auliya through Amir Khusrau but when Nizamuddin Auliya heard that the Sultan was about to come, he moved to Ajodhan. When Alauddin asked him to meet, then Shaikh replied: “There are two doors in my home, if the Sultan comes from one door, I will go out by another.” He was also known as ‘Mehboob-i-Ilahi.’

s: When Jalaluddin Khalji tried to meet Nizamuddin Auliya through Amir Khusrau, where did the saint move?
x: Nizamuddin Auliya never visited Sultans' courts and moved to Ajodhan to avoid Jalaluddin.

s: Whose conversations (malfuzat) does Fawaid-ul-Fuad record?
x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad, compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi, records Nizamuddin Auliya's conversations.

s: Which of the following musical instruments is not of Indo-Islamic origin?
x: Turkic people brought several instruments like Rabab and Sarangi and a new methodology of music and musical instruments with them. The present Sitar was invented by Khusrau. The credit for inventing Tabla goes to Amir Khusrau. M.P.P.S.C. has marked option (d) as the correct answer which is wrong.

s: ‘Tabla’ was introduced by :
x: Amir Khusrau’s real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau. He was a great scholar and poet of his time. He was the first author who used Hindi (Hindavi) phrases and words. The musical instruments like Tabla and Sitar were invented by Amir Khusrau in the 13th/14th century.

s: Musical instrument sitar is the combination of:
x: A musical instrument called Sitar was invented by Amir Khusrau. It combined the features of the old Indian Veena and the Iranian Tambura.

s: Which among the following musical instruments is the finest example of Hindu-Muslim harmony in musical instruments?
x: Indian music motivated Muslim society to be passionate about music. Consequently, Amir Khusrau emerged as a great musician during Sultanate period. He invented ‘Sitar’ with a combination of Irani Tamboora and Indian Veena. He combined some Indian and Persian melodies elegantly and introduced some new melody styles like Iman, Zilf, Sajgari, etc.

s: Which is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music (1375)?
x: The Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music; it is not Amir Khusrau's work.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rag Vibodh — Raja Man Singh Tomar
x: Aiman (Yaman), along with Zilaf and Sazgiri, is a raga traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau. Rag Vibodh is by Somnath, Man Kautuhal by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior, and Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music, not Barani's work.

s: With whom is the music treatise Man Kautuhal associated?
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
x: Man Kautuhal is associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior; Rag Vibodh is by Somnath.

s: Which Sufi order popularised sama and institutionalised qawwali in its khanqahs?
x: The Chishtis popularised sama, and qawwali was institutionalised in Chishti khanqahs using Indian ragas.

s: Who wrote the music treatise Rag Vibodh?
x: Rag Vibodh is by Somnath; Man Kautuhal is linked to Raja Man Singh Tomar.

s: Who among the following is credited with starting the qaul and tarana forms of music?
x: Amir Khusrau is credited with qawwali and with starting qaul, qalbana, tarana and khayal.

s: Who among the following had translated Chintamani Bhatt’s Sanskrit text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it the title ‘Tutinama’?
x: Khwaza Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi translated Chintamani Bhatt’s text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it title 'Tutinama'. Nakhshabi was a 14th-century Persian Physician and Sufisaint who migrated to Badayun (UP).

s: Which ruler is associated with the Persian translation of the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini?
x: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir is associated with translating the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini into Persian.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Razmnama — Persian translation of Suka Saptati
Sringaramanjari — translated into Sanskrit by Shay Akbar
Kalila wa Dimna — Persian version of Panchatantra
Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi — Sanskrit texts from Jwalamukhi temple
x: Razmnama was the Persian translation of the Mahabharata, whereas Suka Saptati was translated as Tutinama.

s: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi was based on the Sanskrit texts of which temple?
x: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi translated Sanskrit texts of the Jwalamukhi temple at Nagarkot under Firoz Tughlaq.

s: Who translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit?
x: Shay Akbar made the reverse translation of Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit.

s: Tutinama of Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi was a Persian translation of which Sanskrit text?
x: Nakhshabi rendered Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati into Persian as the Tutinama in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's time.

s: What is the Razmnama?
o: Persian translation of the Suka Saptati
x: The Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata of the Mughal period.

s: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian version of which work?
x: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian Panchatantra.

s: Who wrote Chandayan, the Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379?
x: Chandayan, an Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379, was written by Mulla Daud.

s: Who wrote Fawaid-ul-Fuad?
x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad is by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Qutban wrote Mrigavati.

s: Who wrote Mrigavati, a Sufi premakhyan?
x: Mrigavati is by Qutban; Chandayan is by Mulla Daud and Padmavat by Jayasi.

s: Ghulam Ali, who translated Padmavat into Urdu, was the court poet of which ruler?
x: Ghulam Ali, court poet of Tana Shah, translated Padmavat into Urdu.

s: The term ‘Apabhramsa’ was used in medieval Sanskrit text to denote
o: early forms of some of the modern Indian language.
x: Apabhramsa denotes the early forms of the modern Indian languages, which grew out of Prakrit. The notes do not cover this.

s: Which was the official language in the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Persian was the elite language of administration in the Sultanate. Urdu grew in camps and bazaars and was not the official language.

s: In the Qutb Shahi kingdom, which language was used among the people and in revenue records?
x: Telugu was used among the people and in revenue records; Persian was used at court and Dakhni Urdu in camps and bazaars.

s: Which Qutb Shahi rulers first issued farmans in Telugu?
o: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah
Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Abul Hasan Tana Shah and Kumara Kampana
Mir Momin Astarabadi and Abdullah Qutb Shah
x: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah are identified as the first Qutb Shahi rulers to issue farmans in Telugu.

s: Addanki Gangadhara occupies an important place in Telugu literary history because he was the first poet to:
o: Dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan
Compose the first Dakhni Urdu diwan
Write a Kannada account of Warangal’s conquest
x: Addanki Gangadhara was the first poet to dedicate a Telugu work, Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam, to a Muslim Sultan, Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

s: What is the Deccan form of Urdu known as?
x: Hindavi grew into Urdu in camps and bazaars; its Deccan form is Dakhni.

s: To whom did Addanki Gangadhara dedicate Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam?
x: Addanki Gangadhara was the first to dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan, Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

s: Which statement regarding Ferishta’s account is correct?
o: It calls Telangana ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323.
It calls Vijayanagara ‘Motupalli’ and describes its fall in 1443.
It calls Bengal ‘Tilang’ and describes its conquest in 1552.
It calls Delhi ‘Tilang’ and describes the rise of the Bahmani kingdom in 1620.
x: Ferishta refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323. The other options substitute incorrect places, events or dates.

s: Which group of writers is specifically associated with accounts of the fall of Warangal in 1323?
o: Kumara Kampana, Gona Budda Reddy and Kase Siddhappa
x: Isami, Barani and Ferishta describe the fall of Warangal in 1323.

s: Who wrote Kasi Khandam?
x: Kasi Khandam is Srinatha's work; Errana completed the Aranya Parva and Tikkana rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

s: Who wrote Ranganatha Ramayanam?
x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is by Gona Budda Reddy; Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam.

s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana render into Telugu?
x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

s: Who wrote Basava Puranam?
x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote Basava Puranam in the Kakatiya period.

s: Errana of the Reddi period completed which parva of the Mahabharata?
x: Errana completed the Aranya Parva.

s: Who wrote the Nirvachanottara Ramayanam?
x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

s: Who is the author of Sringara Naishadham?
x: Srinatha of the Reddi period wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kasi Khandam.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Tughluqnama is by Amir Khusrau; Ibn Battuta's work is the Rihla.

s: Who among the following established independent Muslim rule in Malwa?
x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded independent Malwa; Hoshang Shah only moved the capital to Mandu.

s: Which ruler unified Bengal in 1342 and made Pandua his capital?
x: Haji Ilyas, who assumed the title Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah, unified Bengal in 1342 and established Pandua as his capital.

s: Who moved the capital of Malwa from Dhar to Mandu?
x: Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu; Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and Mahmud Khalji founded the Khalji line.

s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Gujarat in 1407?
x: Zafar Khan, as Muzaffar Shah I, founded the Gujarat Sultanate in 1407.

s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Malwa in 1401?
x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded the Malwa Sultanate.

s: Who shifted the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom from Gulbarga to Bidar?
x:
Ahmad Shah I Wali (1422–1436 CE) shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in 1425 CE. Bidar soon developed into a major centre of:
• Persian culture
• Architecture
